purpose: Highly targeted Book enrichment focused on long-horizon natural injection-mould maintenance histories and concrete mould-maintenance project records. Exact DOI searches were screened against main and the current PR before admission; broad process papers were deliberately excluded.

candidates.title: Data-Driven Predictive Maintenance of Spare Parts for Smart Manufacturing
candidates.scale: April 2011 to March 2024; 64,020 maintenance notifications; 9,157 unique injection moulds; 2,553 unique spare parts
data: maintenance notification records containing injection-mould IDs, maintained spare parts, shot counts at notification time and maintenance dates
mould master data containing plastic requirements, specifications and production capability
analysis focused on gate bushes and centre units because of cost and lead-time importance
target defined as shots until next maintenance rather than calendar age
shot intervals spanning thousands to millions between maintenance events
final classification datasets of 981 gate-bush instances and 605 centre-unit instances
Random Forest test accuracy 69.59% for gate bushes and 69.23% for centre units
0-49-day Random Forest precision 0.82 for gate bushes and 0.88 for centre units
paper explicitly reports data-quality limitations including mixed cleaning/maintenance records, duplicate entries, free-text information loss and lack of component-state information
candidates.rightsState: public conference PDF; proceedings state © 2025 ESREL SRA-E 2025 Organizers, all rights reserved. Treat the industrial dataset as non-public and use only factual aggregate findings with original Book diagrams/tables.
candidates.value: The strongest long-horizon natural mould-maintenance history identified in this programme: it connects mould identity, component maintenance, shot count and date across thousands of moulds over roughly thirteen years, moving the remaining lifecycle gap from 'history unavailable' to 'history exists but raw/recovery access is missing'.
candidates.limitations: The underlying industrial rows are not established as publicly reusable; records mix different maintenance activities and lack direct component-condition labels. The study does not provide verified before/after part-quality recovery after each intervention, and regression performance was weak, so its model outputs must not be presented as universal maintenance limits.

candidates.title: Knowledge-based Estimation of Maintenance Time for Complex Engineered-to-Order Products Based on KPIs Monitoring: A PSS Approach
candidates.scale: real-life mould-maintenance projects from a European mould-making SME
data: historical maintenance-project repository used for Case-Based Reasoning
mould maintenance attributes including typical failures, cycle rate and year of mould manufacture
product attributes including cavity count and other mould/product descriptors
example comparison includes one new maintenance task and five prior mould cases
reported prior-case cycle rates span approximately 45,000 to 80,000 cycles per week
reported prior-case maintenance times span 128 to 592 hours, equivalent to 16 to 74 days
example moulds contain one or two cavities and manufacturing years from 2003 to 2012
case similarity used to estimate maintenance time rather than relying only on engineer memory
candidates.rightsState: open-access Procedia CIRP article under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; use factual values and create original Book case matrices rather than adapting protected tables/figures.
candidates.value: Adds concrete real-mould maintenance project histories with age, usage, configuration, failure/issues and maintenance-duration context, useful for teaching why maintenance planning should retain structured lifecycle records rather than only the latest repair note.
candidates.limitations: Small illustrative case set and focused on maintenance-time estimation, not physical wear progression or verified post-repair part-quality recovery. Reported hours/days are company- and project-specific and must not become generic planning allowances.
